title: Hold parallel jobs on low free disk and release build output
summary: Before each job (and its verifier) starts in `athena drain`, compare free disk space with the measured size of recent job workspaces. Hold the job if there isn't enough. After each job finishes, delete its regenerable `target/` build output. The audience is the user running `drain` with `[parallel] max_concurrency` above 1, and the verifier who runs the new tests.

defaults_applied.how: New tests cover the hold, the admit, and the cleanup. cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check that the job is actually held and that the files are actually removed, not that types exist.
Prefer a maintained crate for the free-space query, and record the call if one is not used.
The hold gates on measured workspace size, and cleanup releases the disk after each job, so both the cause and the trigger are covered.
Tests include the admit case and the cleanup-removes-something case, so a no-op can't pass.
One focused change in the drain path, with no layout or default changes.
Docs and changelog entries written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: `athena drain` in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs is where parallel job admission happens, through `Drain::work`/`run_job` and the `Steps` trait. I did not read run_job in full.
Admission means starting the producer and also the verifier of each job. Both steps must pass the disk check.
The regenerable build output is the per-job `{job_dir}/target/{side}` directories from athena.toml. Cleanup runs once the job finishes, whether it lands, fails or is rejected.
Thresholds get sensible defaults in code, so athena.toml need not change. If a config knob is added under `[parallel]`, only the schema in config.rs gets an optional field.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs gives the drain a fake free-space reading below the measured recent workspace size. It asserts the job and its verifier are not started (held), and the report or UI says the hold was for disk. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
A new test with a fake reading above the needed space asserts the job is admitted and runs. This shows the hold is conditional and not a blanket block. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.

A new test asserts that cleanup of a finished job's regenerable build output (its `target/{side}` directories) runs after the job ends. It checks a fake or temporary directory is gone, and that non-regenerable job files (records, logs, snapshots) remain. Run `cargo test`.

The required space is derived from measured sizes of recent job workspaces on disk (for example the largest or a high percentile of the last N). It is not a hard-coded constant alone, and a fallback is documented for when there are no measurements yet.

The disk check sits where both the producer and the verifier are admitted, in every concurrency mode. A held job waits or is re-queued, and is not counted as failed, so it does not trip the repeated-failure stop.

The free-space reading and workspace sizes sit behind a seam the tests can fake, in the same style as the existing `Steps` fakes. Production code reads the real filesystem. A maintained crate is used for the free-space query, or the choice to hand-roll it is recorded.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass. Existing drain tests behave unchanged with `max_concurrency` 1.
CHANGELOG.md, and the parallel-jobs design doc if touched, describe the disk hold and the cleanup in plain words for an outside reader. They also name the thresholds and how to configure them.

out_of_scope: Changing the per-job CARGO_TARGET_DIR layout (D46) or sharing target directories between jobs
Deleting records/, logs, or anything not regenerable
Disk quotas, per-user limits, or non-Linux free-space heuristics beyond what the chosen crate gives
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass odds than the reference. The change touches the concurrent drain path, needs new fakes in the Steps trait, and the cleanup semantics are ambiguous.
